name: stoken
desc: Tokencode generator compatible with RSA SecurID 128-bit (AES)
why: Generates RSA SecurID tokencodes from a seed, a neat look inside a proprietary token scheme, though the crypto is ordinary.

brief.what_it_is: stoken is a software tokencode generator for Linux and UNIX that is compatible with RSA SecurID 128-bit (AES) tokens. You import a token from a raw seed string or from an sdtid XML file, and it produces the one-time code you type when logging in. The project ships a command-line tool (stoken), a GTK+ GUI (stoken-gui) with cut and paste, and a shared library (libstoken) that other software can call to generate codes on demand.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a Linux and UNIX alternative to the proprietary RSA SecurID software token, with the blind and other disabled users explicitly in mind as people it helps get past hurdles in login systems. It also says plainly that it is a hobbyist project, not affiliated with or endorsed by RSA Security.
brief.how_it_works: You import a token once, either as a raw string such as 2000123456... or as an sdtid file, and stoken can prompt for an optional password so the seed is encrypted on disk. Each run of stoken tokencode then derives the current code from that seed, and --next shows the following one. If the token needs a PIN, stoken prompts for it, or you can cache it in ~/.stokenrc, which the README calls much less secure. The README says modern OpenConnect links against libstoken and can send the generated code as the password.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the README lists these dependencies for a source build: libtomcrypt or nettle, libxml2, and libgtk3.0 (only for stoken-gui). Building from Git needs autoconf, automake and libtool, plus ./autogen.sh first. A release tarball skips autogen. First run is an import step: you supply the token string or sdtid file, then optionally set a password for the seed and, if the token uses one, a PIN. Source builds on macOS need Xcode command line tools, Homebrew packages (nettle, pkg-config, gtk+3 and others), XQuartz for GTK, and LIBTOOL=glibtool exported. The README's macOS notes were tested on Mavericks 10.9.5.
brief.standout: It reimplements a proprietary two-factor token scheme as a small open tool, and it openly calls out accessibility for blind and disabled users. It also offers a shared library so other programs, such as OpenConnect, can generate codes without a separate app.
brief.status: unknown. The README notes that the default branch was renamed to main on May 17, 2023, which shows the repo was touched then. I did not see a release date or last-commit date on the fetched page, so I can't say whether it is current. The repo is hosted under stoken-dev while the README's clone URL points to cernekee/stoken, and I did not check either repository's activity.
brief.caveats: The Windows build is labeled experimental, not tested or maintained regularly, and its TODO lists missing items: wrong default home directory, no installer, GUI needs assets in the current directory, unmasked password entry, no --random flag, and no charset translation on filenames. The macOS instructions are dated (Mavericks, XQuartz for GTK). Caching a PIN in ~/.stokenrc is explicitly less secure. The project is LGPLv2.1+ and is not affiliated with or endorsed by RSA Security. The README does not cover RSA SecurID token types other than 128-bit AES.
